subtitle: How a Ploughman’s Tongue Carried an Epic

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a village poet facing a hazy battlefield vision
panels.action: Sarala Das stands on a raised village mound, palm-leaf manuscript in hand, as behind him the mist thickens into the ghostly outline of chariots and warriors over an Odia countryside of fields and distant temples.

dialogue.text: In Kapilendra’s war-torn Odisha, Sarala Das, a farmer’s son, dared to reshape the Mahabharata so that even the ploughman could hear the gods in his own tongue.

i18n.hi: कपिलेंद्र के युद्धग्रस्त ओडिशा में किसानपुत्र सारला दास ने महाभारत को यूँ बदला कि हल चलाने वाला भी देवताओं की आवाज़ अपनी ही ज़ुबान में सुन सके।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over riverine countryside and distant city
panels.action: A wide view of fifteenth-century Odia countryside: green paddy fields, meandering river, bullock carts on a dusty track, and far away the walled city of Cuttack with the Gajapati’s palace rising above.

dialogue.text: Mid-fifteenth century Odisha. Gajapati Kapilendra Deva rules from Cuttack, his armies riding from the Ganga in the north to the Kaveri in the south, his banners casting a long shadow over fields and shrines.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी का ओडिशा। कटक से गजपति कपिलेंद्र देव राज करते हैं—फौजें गंगा से कावेरी तक दौड़ती हैं, उनके ध्वज खेतों और देवालयों पर लंबी परछाईं डालते हैं।

panels.shot: slow lateral tracking shot across a temple courtyard
panels.action: Brahmins chant from palm-leaf manuscripts in Sanskrit within a stone temple courtyard, while outside, common villagers linger at the doorway, straining to listen but clearly puzzled and excluded.

dialogue.text: In stone courts and temples, priests chant the Mahabharata in Sanskrit. Inside, kings and scholars nod to the sonorous words; outside, farmers catch only echoes, the meaning veiled behind the language.

i18n.hi: पत्थर के दरबारों और मंदिरों में पंडित संस्कृत में महाभारत गाते हैं। भीतर राजा‑विद्वान सिर हिलाते हैं, बाहर किसान बस ध्वनि सुनते हैं, अर्थ भाषा की ओट में छिपा रहता है।

panels.shot: medium shot at eye-level among farmers
panels.action: Young Sarala Das stands barefoot on a bund between paddy plots, a plough resting nearby, listening to an elderly Brahmin reciting in Sanskrit to a small gathered crowd by the field edge.

dialogue.text: In this world stands Sarala Das, remembered as Adi Kabi, born among cultivators, tied to the plough and the monsoon, hearing of Arjuna and Bhishma in a tongue he cannot read or recite.

i18n.hi: इसी दुनिया में खड़े हैं सारला दास, आदि कवि—किसान घर में जन्मे, हल‑मोंसून से बँधे, अर्जुन‑भीष्म की कथा ऐसी ज़ुबान में सुनते हैं जिसे वे न पढ़ सकते हैं, न सुना सकते हैं।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Sarala Das’s face
panels.action: A close view of Sarala Das’s weathered yet curious face, eyes intense, lips slightly parted as he listens, a few drops of sweat and specks of mud still on his skin from work in the fields.

dialogue.speaker: sarala_das
dialogue.text: If the earth I till is Odia, why must my gods speak only in Sanskrit?

i18n.hi: जब मिट्टी ओड़िया है, तो मेरे देवता सिर्फ़ संस्कृत में क्यों बोलें?

panels.shot: interior medium shot in a modest village house
panels.action: Inside a simple mud-walled house lit by an oil lamp, Sarala Das bends over a palm-leaf, stylus in hand, scratching careful lines as a faint outline of Lord Jagannath’s wheel hangs on the wall behind him.

dialogue.text: Later, in his own verses, he calls himself untrained in Sanskrit. Yet he listens, remembers, imagines. At night, under a flickering lamp, he sets his hand to palm-leaf, shaping epic tales in Odia words.

i18n.hi: बाद में अपने ही पदों में कहते हैं, मैं संस्कृत में अनपढ़ हूँ। पर कान खुला रखते हैं, याद रखते हैं, कल्पना करते हैं। रात को टिमटिमाती बाती तले ताड़पत्र पर हाथ चलाते हैं, ओड़िया शब्दों में महाकथा गढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: angled over-the-shoulder close-up of the palm leaf
panels.action: From behind his shoulder we see neat Odia letters etched in Dandi chanda metre on the palm-leaf, the lines marching in rhythmic clusters, while his hand pauses mid-stroke, hovering over the next word.

dialogue.text: He does not simply translate. He rebuilds the Mahabharata in Dandi chanda, a metre dear to local ears, so that its rhythm can roll like the carts on village roads and the waves at Puri’s shore.

i18n.hi: वह केवल अनुवाद नहीं करते। दांड़ी छंद में नया महाभारत रचते हैं, जो स्थानीय कानों का चहेता है, ताकि उसकी लय गाँव की बैलगाड़ियों और पुरी की लहरों सी गूँजे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sarala Das as he speaks to an unseen listener
panels.action: Sarala Das sits on a low wooden stool, stylus resting in his fingers, as he turns his head slightly toward the doorway, as if speaking to someone outside, his face a mix of humility and resolve.

dialogue.speaker: sarala_das
dialogue.text: I am a chasa, a tiller, not a pandit. But this land deserves an epic in its own speech.

i18n.hi: मैं चासा हूँ, हलवाहा हूँ, पंडित नहीं। पर इस धरती को अपना महाकाव्य अपनी बोली में चाहिए।

panels.shot: wide village scene with gathering peasants
panels.action: On a threshing floor at dusk, a circle of farmers, women, and children sits around Sarala Das, who holds a palm-leaf and gestures toward the nearby fields and a distant hill while he recites.

dialogue.text: As his Sarala Mahabharata grows, the world of the Pandavas shifts. Rivers and forests of Odisha enter the story, local hills stand in for distant places, so that a farmer can point and say, ‘The war passed here.’

i18n.hi: ज्यों‑ज्यों सरला महाभारत फैलता है, पांडवों की दुनिया बदलती जाती है। ओडिशा की नदियाँ‑जंगल भीतर उतरते हैं, स्थानीय पहाड़ दूर देशों की जगह लेते हैं, ताकि किसान कह सके—देख, युद्ध यहीं से गुज़रा।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on a single attentive farmer in the crowd
panels.action: One middle-aged farmer in a coarse cotton cloth leans forward, eyes wide, as Sarala Das describes a battle, his gaze glancing from the poet to the horizon where lightning flickers over the fields.

dialogue.text: The old Sanskrit epic had dwelt in distant skies and royal courts. Now, in his telling, the thunder of Kurukshetra echoes in the monsoon over Jagatsinghpur, and Yudhishthira’s doubt sounds like the farmer’s own.

i18n.hi: पुराना संस्कृत महाकाव्य राजमहलों और दूर आसमानों में बसता था। अब उनकी जुबानी कुरुक्षेत्र की गड़गड़ाहट जगतसिंहपुर की बारिश में गूँजती है, युधिष्ठिर की शंका किसान की अपनी सी लगती है।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot linking temple and fields
panels.action: The scene frames a small village shrine with a wooden image of Jagannath, beyond which stretch the fields where Sarala Das stands reading aloud, the temple flag fluttering above both shrine and listeners.

dialogue.text: Through all his lines, another presence runs: Lord Jagannath of Puri. In Sarala’s Mahabharata, devotion rises not only to Krishna of Sanskrit lore, but to the dark wooden lord who watches over Odia fields.

i18n.hi: उनकी हर पंक्ति में एक और उपस्थिति बहती है—पुरी के भगवान जगन्नाथ की। सरला के महाभारत में भक्ति सिर्फ़ संस्कृत के कृष्ण तक नहीं रुकती, वह काले काष्ठ विग्रह तक उठती है जो ओड़िया खेतों पर नज़र रखे बैठा है।

panels.shot: cut-in close-up of his lips and the listening crowd
panels.action: His lips move mid-verse, the crowd held in stillness, a woman clutching her child, a young boy sitting atop a grain basket, everyone caught in the spell of the familiar cadence and vocabulary.

dialogue.text: He scatters folk idiom through the epic, proverbs from the plough and the hearth, weaving them into Bhishma’s counsel and Draupadi’s fury, so that wisdom long spoken in courtyards now rings in the voices of heroes.

i18n.hi: वह लोक कहावतें हर ओर बिखेर देते हैं—हल और चूल्हे की कहन लेकर, उन्हें भीष्म की नसीहत और द्रौपदी के क्रोध में पिरोते हैं, ताकि आँगनों की पुरानी सूझ अब नायकों की आवाज़ में बज उठे।

panels.shot: interior shot of a scholar’s chamber
panels.action: In a darker interior lined with stacked palm-leaves, an older Brahmin scholar reads a leaf of Sarala’s work by lamplight, brows furrowed in concentration, while a younger student peers curiously over his shoulder.

dialogue.text: Not all are sure what to make of this. Some see a farmer-turned-poet daring to handle sacred material. But others sense a new path: scriptural story carried by vernacular song, a bridge between script and soil.

i18n.hi: सबको समझ नहीं आता इसे क्या मानें। किसी की नज़र में किसान‑कवि पवित्र कथा से खिलवाड़ कर रहा है। पर कुछ को लगता है—यह नया रास्ता है, शास्त्र की कथा लोकगीत पर सवार, अक्षर और मिट्टी के बीच पुल बनती हुई।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot dissolving between three scenes
panels.action: A composite panel shows Sarala Das reciting in one village, then another bard reading his text in a different hamlet, and finally a scribe copying his palm-leaf, all linked by the same flowing Odia verses.

dialogue.text: His project does not end with one book. Alongside the Mahabharata, he composes the Vilanka Ramayana and Chandi Purana, building a wide Odia cosmos where Ram, Devi, and the Pandavas all speak in the people’s tongue.

i18n.hi: उनका सफ़र एक किताब पर नहीं रुकता। महाभारत के साथ‑साथ वे वीलंका रामायण और चंडी पुराण रचते हैं, एक विराट ओड़िया ब्रह्मांड जहाँ राम, देवी और पांडव सब जनता की ज़ुबान में बोलते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot with Sarala Das pausing while writing
panels.action: Back in his modest home, an older Sarala Das pauses over a new manuscript, his hair flecked with grey, as outside the doorway a young boy holding a plough-stick listens, half-hidden, eager and shy.

dialogue.speaker: sarala_das
dialogue.text: These leaves are for you, child of the field. May you never stand outside the story again.

i18n.hi: ये पत्ते तुम्हारे लिए हैं, खेत के बच्चे। अब तुम कभी कथा के बाहर खड़े न रहो।

panels.shot: time-lapse style bird’s-eye over changing countryside
panels.action: A high view shows the same village landscape slowly shifting through time: huts replaced by tiled houses, more temples, different dress, yet still a group gathered under a tree around a storyteller with palm-leaves.

dialogue.text: Long after Kapilendra’s conquests fade and new rulers carve up the land, Sarala’s Odia verses travel from leaf to leaf, performer to performer, carrying stories that have learned the curve of the local tongue.

i18n.hi: कपिलेंद्र की फ़तहें मुरझा जाती हैं, नए राजा ज़मीन बाँट लेते हैं, पर सारला की ओड़िया पंक्तियाँ ताड़पत्र से ताड़पत्र, गवैए से गवैए तक चलती हैं, कहानियाँ लेकर जो स्थानीय ज़ुबान की मोड़‑तोड़ सीख चुकी हैं।

panels.shot: interior of a modern archive or library
panels.action: A modern scholar’s hands gently turn the brittle pages of an old palm-leaf manuscript inside an archive, the script faint but clear, while light from a barred window falls across the text.

dialogue.text: In our time, editors gather his scattered leaves, scholars compare his work with other regional Mahabharatas, and see in him not a mere translator, but a creator who made new history in his own language.

i18n.hi: हमारे समय में संपादक उनकी बिखरी पत्तियाँ समेटते हैं, विद्वान उनकी तुलना अन्य प्रांतीय महाभारतों से करते हैं, और उनमें सिर्फ़ अनुवादक नहीं, वह रचनाकार देखते हैं जिसने अपनी भाषा में नया इतिहास गढ़ा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sarala Das facing a single farmer listener
panels.action: We return to a simple scene: Sarala Das seated under a tree, the sun low, as he looks directly at a single farmer sitting across from him, their knees almost touching, the vastness of the epic shrinking into this shared space.

dialogue.text: History remembers him as Adi Kabi, the first great poet of Odia. Yet his greatness lies also in this: he dared to let a farmer’s everyday words hold the weight of an epic and the gaze of the divine.

i18n.hi: इतिहास उन्हें आदि कवि, ओड़िया का प्रथम महाकवि कहता है। पर उनकी सच्ची महत्ता इसमें भी है कि उन्होंने किसान की रोज़मर्रा की बातों को महाकाव्य का भार और देवदृष्टि दोनों सँभालने दिया।
